title: Minus tide
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: A minus tide. The bay goes out farther than Wood has seen it: the flats in long bands to the channel. The uncle read it off the table a week ago. Wood draws the bands and runs out of pad before he runs out of mud.

panels.composition: The mudflats at a minus tide from the launch: bands of mud, ribs of water, the channel far out catching the sky, the far shore. Enormous.

image.prompt: a wide Pacific Northwest estuary at an extreme low tide with long bands of mud and thin ribs of water reaching to a distant channel, black and white, no words

panels.composition: WOOD at the launch's edge with the pad. BARNABY at the mud's edge, one paw in.

image.prompt: a young man at the edge of a boat launch drawing while a small dog tests the mud with one paw, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The pad: bands, bands, bands. The bottom edge of the page reached. The mud goes on.

image.prompt: close on a drawing pad filled edge to edge with horizontal bands of mudflat, the drawing running off the bottom, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood turning the pad sideways to keep going. The flats. The strip has met a thing bigger than the page.

image.prompt: a young man turning his drawing pad sideways at the edge of a vast mudflat to keep drawing, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The first time the pad runs out before the mud. The Spring Special was a page; this is a pad.
